note: Part-count budgets, straight from ART-BIBLE §5. A budget is a performance contract and a style contract at once: consistent density across assets is a large part of what makes a world feel authored rather than assembled. FORMAT-SPEC §10 refuses an asset over budget. Under it is a warning, not a refusal — a two-part sign is minimal, not wrong.
class_field: An asset may name its row in `class`. Without one, the widest envelope for its `kind` applies, which still catches the four-hundred-part crate and lets a nine-part prop through. Declaring a class is how an author gets the tight check.
